Railroad Crafts — Track, Car and Cab

BLET, SMART-TD and BMWED

FRA 49 CFR Part 213 track safety standards, Part 214 roadway worker protection, Part 218 blue signal protection of workers and Part 232 brake system safety standards, worked the way BLET, SMART-TD and BMWED train their own crafts to work them

Eight of the jobs a freight railroad runs on every day: the roadway gang's own protection and briefing, a tie and rail change-out with the machines that do the lifting, a switch locked out and proven by gauge, a full air brake test walked car by car, a cut secured on a grade and proven by test, a grade crossing taken down and proven against a shunt, a locomotive proven ready before it moves, and the blue flag that lets two crews share one cut of equipment without either one trusting the other's protection instead of their own.

20 / 20levels at 75+ lessons
1741lessons across the track
120tasks: a station under a condition
0more stations needed to fill it

Every level reaches 75 lessons. A lesson is one station step run under one condition; each level's number is its tasks' steps added up from the station modules.

The ladder

Level 1 is open; each level opens when the one below is passed — every task in one run of it a mastery run. A task opens its station with its condition; the number after each task is its steps.

Roadway Worker Protection & Job Briefing

14 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 5 min

Every job on the railroad starts with the same habit: a briefing everyone actually signs onto, working limits requested and read back, and a watchman posted at a sighting distance worked back from the timetable speed rather than chosen for convenience.

  • union — BLET certification and training for locomotive engineers and trainmen
  • union — BMWED roadway worker training for track and structures maintenance
  • union — SMART Transportation Division training for conductors, trainmen and yardmasters

14 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 5.3 min

Air Brake Test & Train Inspection

15 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 5.3 min

A brake test is walked and looked at car by car — a set confirmed by eye, not trusted from a gauge in the cab — because a shoe that never actually seated against the wheel reads exactly like a normal brake pipe pressure until somebody looks.

  • union — BLET certification and training for locomotive engineers and trainmen
  • union — BMWED roadway worker training for track and structures maintenance
  • union — SMART Transportation Division training for conductors, trainmen and yardmasters

Hand Brake & Securement on a Grade

14 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 5.3 min

A cut left standing on a grade is held by hand brakes proven by a push-pull test with the air released, never assumed from a count of turns on a wheel, with chocks behind them for the one thing a hand brake alone cannot promise.

  • union — BLET certification and training for locomotive engineers and trainmen
  • union — SMART Transportation Division training for conductors, trainmen and yardmasters

Crossing Signal Maintenance & Flagging

15 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 5.5 min

Taking a grade crossing's automatic protection down for a test means the road gets protected by hand for as long as the gates and lights cannot be trusted, and the crossing is proven with a real shunt before it goes back to drivers who never knew it was down.

  • union — BLET certification and training for locomotive engineers and trainmen
  • union — BMWED roadway worker training for track and structures maintenance
  • union — SMART Transportation Division training for conductors, trainmen and yardmasters

Locomotive Cab Startup & Alerter

14 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 5.5 min

A locomotive gets a walk-around before it gets a cab, both brakes tested before the first mile, and the alerter answered on its own schedule for the whole trip because it is the one device built to notice an engineer who has stopped noticing anything else.

  • union — BLET certification and training for locomotive engineers and trainmen
  • union — SMART Transportation Division training for conductors, trainmen and yardmasters

Blue Flag Protection in the Yard

15 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 5.3 min

Two crews sharing one cut of equipment both need their own blue flag at every point it could be moved from, because a flag protects the worker who displayed it — never the next person who assumes it also covers them.

  • union — BLET certification and training for locomotive engineers and trainmen
  • union — BMWED roadway worker training for track and structures maintenance
  • union — SMART Transportation Division training for conductors, trainmen and yardmasters

Standards evidenced

Registry entries (tools/standards.json) that a task's own source cites and that govern its category, with the levels that evidence each. Evidencing readiness against a standard is not a licence or a certification issued by its body.

BodyStandardLevels

What it proves

Competency: Protect, inspect and secure track, rolling stock and a locomotive under working limits

Demonstrated with a mastery run on 4 of its 8 stations, against FRA 49 CFR 214 Subpart C Roadway worker protection; FRA 49 CFR 218 Subpart B Blue signal protection of workers; FRA 49 CFR 232 Brake system safety standards for freight and other non-passenger trains; union BMWED roadway worker training for track and structures maintenance.

Badges

Each passed level earns an Open Badges 2.0 assertion naming the level, its tasks and their conditions, its lessons and the standards it evidences, with the attempts behind it as evidence, and sends an xAPI statement. Passing level 20, the capstone, climbs the whole track.

A run demonstrates mastery when it earns two or more stars, records zero unsafe actions, answers every interruption it was given, and finishes within 1.5 times the station's par time. One mastery run on enough of a competency's stations earns "demonstrated"; mastery runs on three different days earn "consistent". No other rule earns a competency.

Certification the work leads to: FRA 49 CFR Part 213 track safety standards, Part 214 roadway worker protection, Part 218 blue signal protection of workers and Part 232 brake system safety standards, worked the way BLET, SMART-TD and BMWED train their own crafts to work them. No level claims apprenticeship hours: no registry entry states an equivalence.

Generated from the programme's station modules: lesson counts are read, not typed. The rules are in tools/briefs/ladder-brief.md and the full table in docs/ladders.md.
